items.context: @CoinDesk (4.070.218 seguidores), en inglés: el trader @blknoiz06 confirma que hackearon su wallet; sospecha acceso no autorizado a su terminal de trading Bullpen, donde tenía guardada su clave privada; se vendieron ~$2M en memecoins y $ANSEM cayó 39% en el día. Publicado hace ~47 min: 15.537 vistas, 28 likes, 5 reposts, 18 respuestas (creciendo). Ángulo: custodia / clave privada en software conectado.
items.suggested_text:
The detail that matters isn't the $2M, it's where the key lived. A private key imported into a trading terminal is a hot key by definition: it sits on an online machine, inside third-party software, and that software can sign whatever it's told to. From that point on, the wallet is only as safe as the weakest piece of that stack.

That's the trade-off many active traders accept without saying it out loud: speed and convenience in exchange for an attack surface they don't control. Keys that never touch an internet-connected device remove that whole category of failure, which is the logic behind air-gapped signing.

What makes these incidents so hard to learn from is that nothing looks wrong until the moment it already is. https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526
